This work details the calibration pipeline, including quality control tests, and the evaluation of astrometric residuals against the Gaia DR3 catalogue and internal consistency metrics based on data encompassing more than one year of Euclid operation: the achieved accuracy is 30 mas for 97% of the total area, thus exceeding the requirements for Data Release 1. For the remaining 3%, accuracy declines due to a persistence correction issue: a method to correct the issue is presented. Furthermore, we discuss the stability of the solution over time, its dependence on source properties and instrument configuration, and outline the improvements planned for future Euclid data releases to enhance the astrometric calibration accuracy and efficiency.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.16504.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
arxiv.org/abs/2611.16504.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.16504v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.19308.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
arxiv.org/abs/2611.19308.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.19308v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpost\sigma$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipost\sigma$ and lies $\vnsplanckpost\sigma$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.20300.title: Faster $\chi^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
arxiv.org/abs/2611.20300.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.20300v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $\chi^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.20884.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
arxiv.org/abs/2611.20884.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.20884v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097.title: Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension
arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097.excerpt:
arXiv:2411.08097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present a new class of interacting dark sector models that can address the Hubble tension. Interacting dark radiation (DR) has previously been put forward as a solution to the problem, but this proposal is disfavored by the high-$\ell$ cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We modify this basic framework by introducing a subcomponent of dark matter (DM) that interacts strongly with the DR, so that together they constitute a tightly coupled fluid at early times. We show that if this subcomponent decouples from the interacting DR during the CMB epoch, the $\ell$ modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling are impacted differently from those that entered after, allowing a solution to the problem. We present a model that realizes this framework, which we dub "New Atomic Dark Matter", or nuADaM, in which the interacting dark matter (iDM) subcomponent is composed of dark atoms, and dark "neutrinos" with long-range interactions contribute to the DR, hence the name of the model. This iDM subcomponent is acoustic at early times but decouples from the DR following dark recombination. In contrast to conventional atomic dark matter (ADM) models, the dark photon is part of a richer DR sector, which ensures that it continues to be self-interacting even after recombination. We show that this model admits a significantly larger value of $H_0$ than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$ when fit to CMB and BAO data, while maintaining a comparable goodness of fit. Once the SHOES data set is included, it provides a significantly better fit than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2502.04374.title: The Numerics of VMEC++
arxiv.org/abs/2502.04374.excerpt:
arXiv:2502.04374v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: VMEC++ is a Python-friendly, from-scratch reimplementation in C++ of the Variational Moments Equilibrium Code (VMEC), a fixed- and free-boundary ideal-MHD equilibrium solver for stellarators and tokamaks. The first VMEC implementation was written by Steven P. Hirshman and colleagues in the 1980s and 1990s and its latest Fortran incarnation (PARVMEC, https://github.com/ORNL-Fusion/PARVMEC) is widely used in stellarator optimization systems. Our work improves on previous implementations with regard to various critical aspects: special care has been put in providing an idiomatic Python experience, from installation to actual usage; VMEC++ has a zero-crash policy; it supports inputs in the classic INDATA format as well as friendlier JSON files. VMEC++ execution times are typically less than or equal to previous implementations, and time to convergence can be decreased dramatically by leveraging its hot-restart feature: by providing the output of a VMEC++ run as initial state for a subsequent one, VMEC++ is initialized using the previously converged equilibrium. This can dramatically decrease runtimes when running on many similar magnetic configurations as it typically happens in stellarator optimization pipelines. On the flip side, some features of the original Fortran VMEC implementation are not yet available in VMEC++, such as support for non-stellarator-symmetric configurations. This contribution presents the internal numerics of the open-source VMEC++ package publicly for the first time.

arxiv.org/abs/2509.14701.title: Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
arxiv.org/abs/2509.14701.excerpt:
arXiv:2509.14701v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.06090.title: Posterior Predictive Checks for Gravitational-wave Populations: Limitations and Improvements
arxiv.org/abs/2604.06090.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.06090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: When selecting a model to characterize an astrophysical population, it is crucial to assess whether that model fits the data and, if not, how it can be improved. To this end, posterior predictive checks (PPCs) are a widely-used statistical test of model fit when inferring gravitational-wave source populations. However, PPCs exhibit limitations when assessing single-event parameters with large measurement uncertainty, like the spin tilt angles of the binary black holes (BBHs) observable with the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors. When single-event inference is prior-dominated, traditional PPCs fail to flag even very poor model fits. In this work, we assess the efficacy of various alternative PPCs on poorly-constrained parameters. We compare PPCs conducted on event- vs. data-level parameters (e.g. posterior samples vs. maximum likelihood points), and explore two additional event-level PPCs: partial predictive checks and split predictive checks. Independent of measurement uncertainty, we find that PPCs on maximum likelihood parameters are always more discerning of model misspecification than any event-level PPC. However, when investigating simulated GWTC-3.0-like catalogs, none of the alternative PPCs show significant improvement over those traditionally used, indicating that at that sensitivity, any limited information in the data about spin tilts is insufficient to diagnose model misspecification. Finally, we apply our suite of PPCs to the spin magnitude and tilt distributions inferred in the most recent LVK catalog, GWTC-4.0. We conclude that the Gaussian Component Spins model used therein under-predicts BBHs with large spin magnitudes and over-predicts those with perfectly anti-aligned tilts.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.21755.title: Quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with nontrivial sound speed in inflation
arxiv.org/abs/2604.21755.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.21755v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with a nontrivial sound speed, utilizing a normalized open two-mode squeezed-state framework. Rather than introducing new observables, our analysis focuses on how a modified sound speed dynamically reshapes the Schr\"odinger evolution of the squeezing parameters ($r_k$ and $\phi_k$). We demonstrate how these dynamical changes are inherited by the reduced density matrix of the observable sector. By employing a sound-speed-resonance parametrization, we derive and evaluate the purity, von Neumann entropy, R\'enyi entropies, and logarithmic negativity. We introduce a bounded variable $x = \tanh r_k$ and perform numerical simulations within the inflationary regime. Our numerical results reveal that a nontrivial sound speed significantly suppresses the purity of the reduced state, indicating enhanced effective mixedness. Simultaneously, it strongly amplifies and modulates both the entropic and entanglement diagnostics. More precisely, a nontrivial sound speed postpones the onset of classicality by modulating the decoherence process. Ultimately, we show that a nontrivial sound speed leaves distinct and identifiable quantum-information signatures within the entanglement structure of the early universe.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.14572.title: Modifications of CMB Temperature and Polarization Quadrupole Signals in Thurston Spacetimes
arxiv.org/abs/2605.14572.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.14572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Recent cosmological tests have discovered persistent CMB anomalies in the large-scale isotropy of the universe. Motivated thus by such anomalies that hint at potential departures from statistical isotropy present in recent cosmological observations with the advent of the 'precision cosmology' era, we are led to explore the viability of anisotropic Thurston geometries, described in William Thurston's geometrization conjecture. In this work, we examine the coherent temperature and polarization signals generated in the CMB sky by such geometries. We begin with introducing Thurston spacetimes as our background models and the formalism we use to obtain the patterns. We then construct a set of transfer equations relative to a given background and solve them for each spacetime geometry. We finally discuss the role of spatial curvature in these FLRW limiting models along with their underlying geometry, and attempt to establish some general results on the symmetries of the patterns produced by their time evolution in terms of temperature and Stokes parameters P, Q and U. We show the evolution of temperature and polarization amplitudes in terms of such Stokes parameters at different redshifts and attempt to isolate individual Thurston geometries.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.28275.title: Dark Matter Interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande Antineutrino Excess in $\mathrm{U}(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ model

arxiv.org/abs/2606.01236.title: Improving the resolution of double white dwarf systems with spaceborne gravitational wave observatories using a robust astrophysical prior
arxiv.org/abs/2606.01236.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.01236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Resolving the crowded population of double white dwarf (DWD) binaries in data from spaceborne gravitational wave (GW) observatories (e.g., LISA, Taiji) remains a major analysis challenge. Comparable performance on addressing this problem has been achieved with two main approaches: global fit, in which resolvable sources are estimated simultaneously from the data, and iterative, where sources are estimated one at a time and subtracted out from the data. While the latter is computationally efficient, methods developed under this approach have traditionally followed a frequentist framework that ignores astrophysical priors. This work incorporates a strong astrophysical prior, derived from the mass limits of detached white dwarfs and linking the GW signal frequency $f$ with its time derivative $\dot{f}$, into the iterative \fitalgoname{} pipeline. Applied to simulated LISA and LISA-Taiji network data, the method increases the number of confidently resolved sources by ${\approx}7.3\%$ (LISA-only) and ${\approx}14.6\%$ (network) at matched detection rate, respectively, and improves parameter estimation accuracy.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.15680.title: Assessing the enrichment of heat-producing elements in deep-mantle structures using a directional geoneutrino detector
arxiv.org/abs/2606.15680.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.15680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Determining the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth is critical for understanding the planet's thermal and chemical evolution. A central debate is whether domains in the deep mantle, particularly the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVP), represent anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Variation in the surface flux of geoneutrinos provide a direct probe of Earth's internal radioactivity. However, current continental located detectors measure only the angle-integrated flux, leading to strong spatial trade-offs that substantially limit the ability of practical networks to uniquely resolve mantle compositional heterogeneity. In this study, we quantify the potential of directional geoneutrino detection to overcome this limitation. By evaluating realistic LLVP geometries in the context of the proposed Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD), we demonstrate that resolving the incoming direction of geoneutrinos can substantially improve the precision with which HPE enrichment in LLVPs can be constrained relative to the surrounding mantle, for a range of target angular resolutions envisioned for a future directional geoneutrino detector. These results indicate that future directional geoneutrino measurements could help determine whether LLVP host enhanced HPE abundances and assess their contribution to Earth's radiogenic heat budget. Such measurements would provide a new observational constraint on the chemical heterogeneity of the deep mantle and its role in Earth's long-term thermal evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.20957.title: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects in Non-Radial Relativistic Stellar Perturbations: A Model-Agnostic Formulation and Mode Analysis
arxiv.org/abs/2606.20957.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.20957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present a systematic, model-agnostic analysis of out-of-equilibrium effects, including viscosity and thermal conductivity, in non-radial oscillations of relativistic stars. Extending the Lindblom-Detweiler formalism, we construct, to our knowledge, the first general framework for linear, non-radial relativistic stellar perturbations that incorporates generic nonequilibrium corrections to the perfect-fluid sector in both the even- and odd-parity channels. Our framework is formulated in terms of the tensorial structure and thermodynamic decomposition of generic corrections without relying on any specific constitutive relations, thereby allowing us to elucidate, at a structural level, how these effects enter the perturbation equations and contribute to geometric deformations and fluid fluctuations. As an application, we consider the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun fluid and perturbatively investigate shifts in the frequencies and damping times of modes connected to their perfect-fluid counterparts in the limit of vanishing transport coefficients. We also identify structural features of the closed eigenvalue problem that suggest the possibility of additional mode families. Our formalism provides a unified framework for analyzing how different relativistic fluid theories modify the structure of non-radial stellar perturbations.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.21925.title: From the Early Slope to Curvature: Future Prospects and challenges for Astrophysical Parameter Estimation Using the Core-Collapse Supernova High-Frequency Feature
arxiv.org/abs/2607.21925.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.21925v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) contain both stochastic and deterministic components. Among these, the High-Frequency Feature (HFF), associated with Proto-Neutron Star (PNS) oscillations, has emerged as an observable for probing dense-matter physics. Previous studies of the HFF have primarily focused on its early-time slope as a diagnostic of PNS contraction and its dependence on the nuclear equation of state (EOS). In this work, we investigate recovering higher-order features of the HFF evolution, such as its curvature, from core-collapse supernova numerical simulations. By analyzing 2D and 3D waveforms injected into real interferometric noise, we apply the coherent WaveBurst algorithm in its cWB-XP implementation to reconstruct the HFF of recovered events. Comparing reconstructions at different signal strengths allows us to examine the extent to which the HFF remains accessible beyond its early linear evolution

arxiv.org/abs/2609.10111.title: Multiparameter quantum bounds for entanglement-assisted aperture synthesis
arxiv.org/abs/2609.10111.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.10111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Entanglement-assisted optical interferometry promises diffraction-limited imaging over baselines where light cannot be physically combined, but its estimation-theoretic bounds exist only for a single visibility on one baseline. This work formulates the multiparameter quantum estimation problem for an M-station array. A reduction lemma shows that the multimode quantum Fisher information (QFI) equals the mean photon number times the QFI of a single delocalized photon, making the problem finite-dimensional. The local photon-number superselection rule erases all phase information from the bare state; shared entanglement restores a fraction f(r)=r/(1+r) of the QFI on a baseline supplied with r pairs, a benchmark that applies to every pair of the array. The QFI matrix and its mean Uhlmann curvature show numerically that a point source is measurement-compatible, whereas every extended-source model examined is incompatible; a semidefinite-programming evaluation shows that the Holevo bound exceeds the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative bound by up to ~24% for three stations and by 4-8% for larger arrays and for CHARA. An explicit collective receiver, a numerically optimised global linear-optical network with photon counting, attains a weighted variance within 2-9% of the Holevo bound, over an order of magnitude below an explicit pairwise receiver, and a noisy-resource threshold gives the break-even baseline (~22 km for illustrative parameters) beyond which distributed entanglement beats direct transmission. Finally, allocating a finite entanglement budget has a closed-form proportional (square-root-law) solution for a per-baseline fringe cost, whereas for the source-parameter variance under an explicit photon budget the routing of photons matters far more than the entanglement split. These results recast quantum aperture synthesis as collective multiparameter estimation, illustrated on CHARA.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12719.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12719.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.37198.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.37198.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.37198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.

universetoday.com/articles/esas-hera-pro.title: ESA's Hera Probe Uses "Superhuman" Vision to Inspect NASA's Asteroid Crash Site
universetoday.com/articles/esas-hera-pro.excerpt: Around four years ago, humanity intentionally hit an asteroid. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) was by pretty much all measures a resounding success when it struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos going more than 22,000 kilometers per hour. However, we still don’t know just how much of a success it actually was - DART was a one-way mission with no real way to track the results of the impact close up. Enter Hera, the European Space Agency (ESA) mission that recently arrived in the binary asteroid system. Now, in a press release, ESA has provided some of the best pictures of the binary system since that fateful day four years ago.

9.headline: Ultracold Rubidium Atoms Mimic Schwinger Pair Production
9.summary: Researchers used an optical lattice of ultracold rubidium atoms to simulate the elusive Schwinger effect, revealing how mass and field strength control pair creation.
highlights: Ultracold rubidium atoms were arranged in a one‑dimensional optical lattice to represent a false vacuum
Tuning the simulated particle mass and background electric field altered the observed pair‑production rate
Quantum gas microscope imaging captured real‑time dynamics of the simulated particle‑antiparticle creation

7.headline: Delayed Rise of Lyman Continuum Escape in Bursty High‑Redshift Galaxies
7.summary: Simulations show that Lyman continuum escape fractions peak about 16 Myr after star‑formation bursts, especially in massive early galaxies.
highlights: Typical LyC escape lag is ~16 Myr with peak correlations of 0.4‑0.6 in massive haloes
Delay scales as M★⁻⁰·¹⁹ and Mhalo⁻⁰·²⁷, lengthening for lower‑mass systems
Hα‑to‑UV luminosity ratio retains a delayed link to LyC escape, offering an observable tracer

15.headline: Astrolabe Surrogate Generates Full‑Resolution Cosmology Simulations via Flow Matching
15.summary: Astrolabe uses a flow‑matching transformer to emulate particle‑level cosmology, delivering accurate large‑scale structure without voxel resolution limits.
highlights: Acts directly on 6N phase‑space coordinates of individual particles
Employs a hybrid transformer where each particle cross‑attends to multiscale field tokens
Matches physical flow using approximate COLA coordinates, preserving momentum and mass
Reproduces power spectra, halo mass functions, velocity and density profiles in Lambda‑CDM tests
Generalizes to dark‑acoustic oscillation initial conditions and scales to TNG50‑3‑dark size

8.headline: Scientists Capture Electrons Leaping Across Forbidden Gaps in Graphene
8.summary: Using a photoemission momentum microscope, researchers observed electrons in graphene making Landau‑Zener‑Majorana transitions with up to 100 % probability under intense light.
highlights: Electrons crossed forbidden energy gaps in graphene with transition probabilities reaching 100 %
The experiment combined ultrafast laser pulses with a photoemission momentum microscope to record sub‑cycle electron dynamics
Ultra‑pure, rotated graphene samples from Forschungszentrum Jülich enabled clear observation of the quantum jumps

11.headline: JWST Spectroscopy Reveals Common Mini‑Quenched Galaxies at z > 4
11.summary: Deep 28‑hour NIRSpec/PRISM observations in the OASIS program find that suppressed, mini‑quenched and lulling galaxies constitute a sizable fraction of early low‑mass galaxies.
highlights: Three mini‑quenched galaxies with log(M/Msun)=8.3‑8.9 lie 1.2‑1.7 dex below the star‑forming main sequence
Five lulling galaxies show weak Balmer emission just above the quenching threshold
Suppressed galaxies represent 29% of the sample at z=4‑5.5, with a number density ≈1.6×10⁻³ Mpc⁻³ dex⁻¹
Photometric estimates overstate star‑formation rates, misclassifying most candidates without spectroscopy

12.headline: Topological Analysis of 21‑cm Signal Could Discriminate Competing Cosmologies at z≈10
12.summary: A new study shows that persistent homology of a single 21‑cm brightness slice near redshift 10 can separate models differing in h₀, nₛ, Ωₘ and σ₈ despite thermal noise.
highlights: Persistent homology applied to 21‑cm fields identifies distinct topological signatures for each cosmological parameter set.
Wasserstein distance between persistent diagrams quantifies differences even with realistic instrumental noise.
PERMANOVA tests confirm statistical separability of models across h₀, nₛ, Ωₘ and σ₈ variations.
The redshift range around z=10 emerges as optimal for distinguishing scenarios during the Epoch of Reionization.

6.headline: Uterine Microbiome Linked to IVF Success Rates in Irish Study
6.summary: A DNA sequencing analysis of 29 Irish women suggests diverse uterine bacteria may lower IVF pregnancy odds, highlighting microbiome‑inflammation interplay.
highlights: Researchers at Trinity College Dublin found higher bacterial diversity in uterine samples of women with unsuccessful IVF outcomes.
Lower presence of Lactobacillus and higher levels of other species correlated with reduced pregnancy success.
In vitro exposure of endometrial cells to bacterial butyrate triggered inflammation and weakened cellular barriers.

4.headline: Chandra Reveals Kiloparsec-Scale Jet at Record-Breaking z=6.1
4.summary: Deep 360 ks Chandra observations resolve the distant AGN jet into two X‑ray components, showing a steep photon index and an 18% extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio.
highlights: Extended X‑ray emission splits into two slightly resolved components
Photon index of the jet is Γ = 2.25, steeper than the core’s Γ = 1.86
Extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio reaches 18%
Simulations suggest an AXIS‑like mission could boost photon counts by ~17×

10.headline: 30,000‑Year‑Old DNA Shows Ice Age Europeans Were Far More Connected
10.summary: Ancient DNA from human remains and cave sediments reveals extensive gene flow across Europe 30,000 years ago, overturning the view of isolated Paleolithic groups.
highlights: Genome from a woman at Isturitz Cave combines western, central and eastern European ancestry
Sedimentary DNA from El Mirón Cave (≈22 ka) confirms persistent western ancestry through the Last Glacial Maximum
Genetic modeling dates inter‑regional mixing to 32,500‑31,500 years ago
Evidence from Chufín Cave shows long‑term regional continuity in southwestern Europe

tde_multimessenger_lepto_hadronic.headline: Hidden Engines in Tidal Disruption Events Reveal Multimessenger Signals
tde_multimessenger_lepto_hadronic.summary: New lepto‑hadronic models show that certain tidal disruption events could be simultaneously detectable in MeV‑GeV‑TeV gamma rays and high‑energy neutrinos.
highlights: Hard proton spectra and large minimum proton Lorentz factors boost TeV gamma‑ray and neutrino detectability
AT2019dsg and AT2019ehz can meet CTAO and KM3NeT/ARCA sensitivity in favourable hadronic configurations
ASASSN‑14li is naturally bright in the MeV‑GeV band but constrained by its radio synchrotron emission

ddelens_simulation_suite.headline: New DDELenS Simulations Enable Precise Dark Energy Probes via Weak Lensing
ddelens_simulation_suite.summary: A suite of 128 w₀wₐCDM simulations with massive neutrinos provides tomographic weak‑lensing maps for next‑generation cosmology surveys.
highlights: 128 cosmological runs sample Ωₘ, σ₈, w₀, wₐ using a Sobol sequence
Each run follows 1024³ particles in a 512 h⁻¹ Mpc box with PKDGRAV3
10,000 ray‑traced convergence maps generated for six source redshifts
Covariance matrix built from 100,000 realizations at the fiducial model

wide_binary_gravity_test.headline: Study of 65 Wide Binaries Finds No Gravitational Anomaly at Low Acceleration
wide_binary_gravity_test.summary: A Monte Carlo analysis of 65 wide binary systems shows Newtonian dynamics fully explain their orbits, with no excess velocity at accelerations below 10⁻⁹ m s⁻².
highlights: Orbital solutions were obtained for 65 systems, including 26 newly added twin M‑type binaries.
The low‑acceleration subsample (A_N < 10⁻⁹ m s⁻²) shows eccentricity and periastron distributions matching theoretical
Parallax errors dominate uncertainties, especially affecting inclination and phase determinations.
The boost parameter γ is constrained to 0.95–1.05 (1σ), consistent with pure Newtonian gravity.

20_000_rotation_periods_from_ztf_asas_sn.headline: 20,000 Stellar Rotation Periods Unveiled from ZTF and ASAS‑SN Surveys
20_000_rotation_periods_from_ztf_asas_sn.summary: A new catalog of ~20,000 periodic signals from nearby open clusters and moving groups offers unprecedented ground‑based data on stellar rotation and magnetic braking.
highlights: Catalog contains ~20,000 periodic photometric signals, including rotations, eclipsing binaries, and classical pulsators.
Targets members of open clusters and moving groups within 1.5 kpc, focusing on low‑mass GKM dwarfs.
Data derived from Zwicky Transient Facility and All‑Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae, providing long‑baseline ground‑based
Enables testing of magnetic‑braking models across a broad mass and age range.

2610_27287v1.headline: Gravitational‑Wave Data Could Reveal First‑Order QCD Transitions in Neutron Stars
2610_27287v1.summary: A new formalism shows that upcoming LIGO A+ and A# runs, plus Cosmic Explorer, may detect first‑order QCD phase transitions during neutron‑star inspirals.
highlights: The method uses only inspiral signals from GW170817 and GW190425 to test for phase transitions.
Simulations indicate A+ or A# observations could confirm a first‑order transition within a PhD‑timescale.
Second‑ and third‑order transitions remain indistinguishable from no transition using inspiral data alone.
Cosmic Explorer would dramatically improve sensitivity to subtle equation‑of‑state changes.

arxiv_2610_26936v1.headline: SUBWAYS Reveals Soft X‑Ray Excess Links to Ultra‑Fast Outflows in AGN
arxiv_2610_26936v1.summary: A multiwavelength study of 21 active galactic nuclei shows that the soft X‑ray excess correlates with ultra‑fast outflows and corona properties.
highlights: Two‑coronae model fits broadband emission with warm corona temperatures kTₑ≈0.1‑0.9 keV and photon index Γ>2
Hybrid model required for 9 of 21 AGN, especially 4 of 7 UFO hosts
UFO hosts exhibit lower warm‑corona temperatures and harder hot‑corona spectra
Correlation found between warm‑corona optical depth and UFO outflow velocity

arxiv_2610_27186v1.headline: New Binary Evolution Model Explains Massive Black Hole X‑ray Binaries
arxiv_2610_27186v1.summary: A refined main‑sequence treatment in the COMPAS code shows that non‑conservative case A mass transfer is essential to reproduce observed massive BH‑HMXBs and alters BBH merger properties.
highlights: Non‑conservative case A mass transfer reproduces the high black‑hole masses seen in BH‑HMXBs
Helium‑enriched material transfer during case A is common, affecting accretor structure
The updated model shifts chirp‑mass and mass‑ratio distributions of detectable BBH mergers
Stable mass‑transfer channel now contributes significantly to near‑equal‑mass BBHs

subarcsecond_dual_agn_eris.headline: ERIS Uncovers Six Sub‑Arcsecond Dual AGN and Seven New Lensed Quasars
subarcsecond_dual_agn_eris.summary: Using ERIS‑SPIFFIER on the ESO VLT, astronomers confirmed six dual AGN at 0.2''‑0.9'' separations and discovered seven previously unknown gravitationally lensed quasars.
highlights: 34 Gaia‑selected candidates were observed with R ≈ 5000‑5600 integral‑field spectroscopy
13 systems (≈40 %) resolved into multiple AGN‑like components
Six dual AGN span z = 0.68‑1.57 with velocity offsets Δv ≈ 290‑950 km/s
Seven gravitationally lensed quasars include four doubles and three quadruples, only one previously known

rna_energy_starvation.headline: Excess RNA Harms Mitochondria, Cutting Cellular Energy Supply
rna_energy_starvation.summary: Researchers found that surplus messenger and double‑stranded RNA directly damage mitochondria, reducing ATP production and potentially linking viral infection to cellular energy loss.
highlights: RNA overload impairs mitochondrial respiration without triggering immune pathways
Both viral mRNA and host mRNA can disrupt the electrical balance of mitochondrial membranes
Poxvirus‑infected cells rely on RNA degradation to keep energy production viable

ammonia_hydrogen_phase_equilibria.headline: Ammonia May Rain Inside Uranus and Neptune, New Simulations Show
ammonia_hydrogen_phase_equilibria.summary: Large‑scale machine‑learning molecular dynamics reveal ammonia‑hydrogen phase separation at pressures up to 30 GPa, suggesting ammonia rain in Uranus and Neptune today.
highlights: Critical temperature rises from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa
No phase separation found at 3000‑4000 K up to 100 GPa
Phase boundary intersects published thermal profiles of Uranus and Neptune
Warm sub‑Neptunes like TOI‑270 d remain fully miscible

rejuvenation_breakthrough_reverse_60_yea.headline: Scientists Reverse Over 60 Years of Cellular Aging in Human Blood Cells
rejuvenation_breakthrough_reverse_60_yea.summary: Researchers at the University Hospital of Bonn transformed blood cells from an 80‑year‑old into neural stem cells with a molecular age under 20, resetting epigenetic clocks.
highlights: Blood cells from an 80‑year‑old donor were reprogrammed directly into neural stem cells without a pluripotent intermediate
Molecular age, measured by epigenetic clocks, dropped from ~80 to <20 years over a 100‑day period
Rejuvenation proceeded gradually, allowing detailed tracking of epigenetic changes for more than 50 days
The approach offers a new model for studying age‑related neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s

numerical_shock_broadening_supernova_neu.headline: Numerical Shock Broadening Alters Supernova Neutrino Signals for DUNE
numerical_shock_broadening_supernova_neu.summary: Hydrodynamical simulations spread the supernova shock over several grid zones, artificially increasing adiabaticity of MSW conversion and affecting DUNE event rates.
highlights: Stored shock fronts span 1.6–1.7 grid zones, while a 2.2 km reconstruction mimics a sudden crossing
Ray‑averaged H‑resonance crossing probability $P_H$ rises by 0.44–0.76, median 0.56

A 40 kt argon detector would see a –4.4% change in $
u_e$ charged‑current counts

arxiv_2610_26969.headline: Low‑mass galaxies at z>6 are mostly prolate, study finds using FIREboxHR simulations
arxiv_2610_26969.summary: Analysis of FIREboxHR galaxies shows that early low‑mass systems are predominantly prolate with a notable spheroidal component, challenging common shape‑inference assumptions.
highlights: Prolate shapes dominate for galaxies with log(M★/M⊙)=6.5‑9.5 at z∼6‑15
Intrinsic ellipticity E and triaxiality T follow Johnson SB distributions, while size A is log‑normal
Bayesian forward modeling with a multivariate normal in (logit E,logit T,log A) reproduces particle‑measured shapes better than
Mock JWST/NIRCam images reveal that large samples or strong priors are needed to constrain triaxiality from projected data

arxiv_2610_27005.headline: PSR B0355+54 Shows Nearly All Known Scintillation Arc Types
arxiv_2610_27005.summary: Observations of PSR B0355+54 with the Shanghai Tianma Radio Telescope reveal five arc morphologies across 54 sessions, challenging prior expectations.
highlights: Scintillation arcs detected in 53/53 usable 2.25 GHz observations and 33/49 at 8.60 GHz
Five morphological types identified: forward arcs, inverted arclets, diffuse arcs, diffuse power, irregular structures
Arc curvature variations indicate a dominant scattering screen at fractional distance s≈0.069 near the pulsar
Displaced arclets tracked for 10 h at 8.60 GHz show rapid evolution consistent with small‑scale scattering structures

lightest_neutron_star_binary.headline: Lightest Double Neutron Star Pair Confirms Einstein’s Theory to 1% Accuracy
lightest_neutron_star_binary.summary: Astronomers using FAST measured three relativistic effects in PSR J1856‑0039, showing general relativity matches the system’s motion within about one percent.
highlights: The 2.36‑hour orbit shrinks by roughly 9 feet each year due to gravitational‑wave emission.
The orbital ellipse precesses 17.6 degrees per year, far faster than Mercury’s relativistic drift.
Pulse timing varies by up to half a millisecond as the pulsar’s clock runs slower at different orbital phases.
The two stars weigh 1.3 and 1.19 solar masses, the lowest total mass known for a double neutron‑star system.

pbhs_microlensing_limits.headline: Model Assumptions Can Weaken OGLE Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes
pbhs_microlensing_limits.summary: A new analysis shows that varying Milky Way and LMC halo models can reduce OGLE’s dark‑matter constraints on primordial black holes by up to sixfold.
highlights: Changing Milky Way halo parameters weakens the PBH bound by up to a factor of ~6.
Adjusting the Large Magellanic Cloud halo or stellar lens populations can relax limits by over an order of magnitude in extreme
Primordial clustering further reduces the planetary‑mass PBH constraint by a factor of 3.4–6.
The study recommends quoting dark‑matter limits alongside their modeling assumptions.

2610_30659v1.headline: Gaia DR3 Reveals Bursty Formation of the Milky Way’s High‑α Disk
2610_30659v1.summary: Analysis of ~145,000 Gaia DR3 subgiants shows two distinct age‑metallicity components in the high‑α disk, indicating episodic star formation bursts.
highlights: Dominant component peaks at ~10.6 Gyr with [Fe/H] ≈ ‑0.38.
Older component peaks at ~12.4 Gyr with [Fe/H] ≈ ‑0.79.
Ages align with the proposed Low‑energy‑Kraken‑Heracles accretion event ~12.3 Gyr ago.
Forward‑modelling corrects selection effects and individual uncertainties for ~145,000 subgiants.

pevatron_candidate_hess1702.headline: Chandra Resolves Pulsar Candidate Near Pevatron HESS J1702‑420A
pevatron_candidate_hess1702.summary: New 50.4 ks Chandra ACIS‑I observations split the hard X‑ray source XMMU J170147.3‑421407 into a faint point source Src11 and asymmetric diffuse lobes, suggesting a pulsar wind nebula.
highlights: Src11 (CXO J170144.5-421415) appears as a faint point‑like X‑ray source within the former XMM‑Newton detection
Diffuse emission shows eastern and western lobes with an unusual asymmetric morphology
Machine‑learning classification and spectral analysis favor a pulsar/PWN interpretation
The ~7′ offset from the TeV peak HESS J1702‑420A complicates a definitive association

2610_30879v1.headline: Relativistic Model Reveals Hidden Dynamics in AT2017gfo Kilonova Spectrum
2610_30879v1.summary: A new relativistic dynamical model predicts broken‑power‑law temperature evolution and shows Doppler and light‑travel‑time effects reshape early spectra of the AT2017gfo kilonova.
highlights: Thermal evolution follows a broken power law as ejecta become optically thin
Equal‑arrival‑time surface geometry and Doppler boosting cause significant spectral distortions at velocities ≳ 0.5c
MCMC fitting with a Student’s t likelihood yields ejecta mass, opacity, and velocity estimates for AT2017gfo
Relativistic corrections grow stronger at large viewing angles, altering observed temperatures

ptsd_treatment_remission_2026.headline: FDA-Cleared Personalized Brain Stimulation Shows 68% PTSD Remission in Trial
ptsd_treatment_remission_2026.summary: A new FDA-cleared MeRT system using AI-guided TMS achieved a 52% symptom reduction and 68% remission in an early clinical trial of PTSD patients.
highlights: Personalized brain mapping guided magnetic stimulation yielded a 52% reduction in PTSD symptom scores.
68% of trial participants met remission criteria after five to six weeks of treatment.
The device received FDA Breakthrough Device designation in 2024 and is the first non‑medication option cleared for PTSD.

jwst_exoplanet_lopsided.headline: JWST Maps Lopsided Atmosphere of Hot Jupiter WASP‑17 b
jwst_exoplanet_lopsided.summary: Using JWST’s infrared camera, researchers applied transmission‑string modeling to reveal a dramatically asymmetric atmosphere on the tidally‑locked hot Jupiter WASP‑17 b.
highlights: Morning limb temperature ~858 K, evening limb ~1,522 K, a 650 K difference
Atmospheric radius expands to 1.8 × on the hot evening side
Water vapor and carbon dioxide remain uniform, while methane and sulfur dioxide vary near the poles

kikai_caldera_magma_refill_2026.headline: Fresh Magma Recharges Japan’s Kikai Supervolcano After 7,300‑Year Gap
kikai_caldera_magma_refill_2026.summary: Seismic surveys by Kobe University and JAMSTEC reveal a newly injected magma reservoir beneath Kikai caldera, showing how supervolcanoes rebuild their supply over millennia.
highlights: Underwater seismic surveys identified a large, high‑magma zone directly beneath the ancient eruption site.
Chemical analysis shows the magma differs from the 7,300‑year‑old eruptive material, indicating fresh injection.
The reservoir’s growth aligns with a lava dome that has formed over the past 3,900 years.
Findings suggest similar re‑injection processes may operate beneath Yellowstone and Toba.

stupendously_large_bh_dark_matter_2026.headline: Stupendously Large Black Holes Fail to Explain Dark Matter, Study Shows
stupendously_large_bh_dark_matter_2026.summary: Analysis of the cosmic microwave background shows that black holes over 100 billion solar masses cannot constitute a major fraction of dark matter.
highlights: Researchers examined CMB temperature fluctuations at one part in 100,000.
No evidence of graininess expected from stupendously large black holes was found.
The largest known black hole is ~36 billion solar masses, far below the required >100 billion.
Findings will appear in Physical Review Letters on Oct. 26.

2610_30243v1.headline: Cloud‑Circulation Feedback Shapes WASP‑43b Atmosphere, New Study Shows
2610_30243v1.summary: A combined 3‑D dynamics and 1‑D microphysics model reveals cloudy nightsides and clear daysides on hot Jupiter WASP‑43b, matching JWST data.
highlights: Post‑processing links ADAM‑SPARC GCM with CARMA cloud model and PICASO radiative transfer
Model predicts five condensate species, including silicate clouds, but overestimates opacity
JWST phase‑curve spectra indicate clear dayside and patchy limb clouds on WASP‑43b

hidden_brain_messaging_system.headline: Hidden Messaging System Unveiled in Locus Coeruleus Neurons
hidden_brain_messaging_system.summary: A tiny region of the brainstem, the locus coeruleus, uses distinct neuron pathways to send targeted norepinephrine signals that shape learning, attention and behavior in mice.
highlights: Locus coeruleus neurons project separately to cortex and spinal cord, creating a targeted norepinephrine network rather than a
Dorsal LC cells fire during learning tasks while ventral LC cells rise before animals ignore reward cues
Whole‑brain imaging mapped nearly 35,000 neurons and 400,000 cell profiles, revealing axons up to 70.32 cm long
Findings, published in Nature 2026, could guide more precise therapies for ADHD, depression and Alzheimer’s disease

malaria_parasite_portal.headline: Cryo‑EM Captures Malaria Parasite’s Moving Junction in Action
malaria_parasite_portal.summary: Researchers at Columbia University used cryo‑electron microscopy to visualize the Plasmodium moving junction, revealing how the parasite remodels red blood cell membranes during invasion.
highlights: The team imaged the moving junction at the exact moment of red blood cell entry using cryo‑electron microscopy.
Four protein units form a dense wedge that deforms and reseals the host membrane as the parasite slips through.
An AI‑powered protein‑design platform created an inhibitory protein that blocked invasion in test‑tube experiments.
The findings suggest the moving junction could serve as a drug target for malaria and related apicomplexan diseases.

alpine_zones_greening_northeast_na.headline: Alpine Zones in Northeastern North America Are Greening Rapidly
alpine_zones_greening_northeast_na.summary: Satellite analysis shows 88% of alpine terrain across the White Mountains, Adirondacks and Gaspé Peninsula has become greener since 1984, reshaping plant communities.
highlights: Nearly 1,000 Landsat images from 1984‑2024 reveal greening over 11,352 hectares of alpine area.
88% of the studied alpine region shows significant NDVI increase, with no sites turning browner.
Strong winds on peaks like Mount Washington (231 mph) appear to limit greening, creating uneven patterns.

moon_forming_impact_properties.headline: Crunchy Theia Model Suggests Moon Could Form Directly From Impact
moon_forming_impact_properties.summary: New Astrophysical Journal Letters study shows that modeling Theia with a solid crust can produce a proto‑Moon instead of a debris disk after the Earth collision.
highlights: Researchers at Southwest Research Institute led by Adeene Denton modeled Theia as a solid body colliding with a fluid Earth
A warm, near‑melting Theia produced a single proto‑Moon, whereas a colder, stronger Theia broke into granola‑like fragments
The simulations used a proto‑Earth at 88% of present Earth mass and Theia at 13% of Earth’s mass, matching canonical impact
The paper is peer‑reviewed and published in Astrophysical Journal Letters, highlighting the role of material strength in

mars_canyon_activity.headline: Mars’ Giant Valles Marineris Canyon Still Tectonically Active, Study Shows
mars_canyon_activity.summary: Seismic data from NASA’s InSight lander reveal a strike‑slip marsquake beneath Valles Marineris, proving the canyon’s faults remain active.
highlights: The S0976a event on 25 August 2021 originated 20–40 km below Valles Marineris, showing sideways fault motion.
Models ruled out impact or landslide causes, matching strike‑slip seismic signatures.
Study published in Nature Communications by Imperial College London, Columbia University and collaborators.
Findings suggest long‑term cooling and volcanic stresses can reactivate ancient rift faults on a “stagnant‑lid” planet.

13.headline: Novartis' remibrutinib Cuts MS Relapse Rates by Over a Third
13.summary: In Phase 3 REMODEL‑1 and ‑2 trials, Novartis’ remibrutinib lowered the annualized relapse rate by 35.2% and 31.2% versus Aubagio.
highlights: Remibrutinib achieved a 35.2% reduction in annualized relapse rate in REMODEL‑1.
In REMODEL‑2 the reduction was 31.2% compared with Aubagio.
The drug showed a cleaner safety profile than Roche’s fenebrutinib, which demonstrated >50% reduction but higher adverse events.

bennu_samples_2026.headline: NASA Bennu Samples Reveal Hybrid Birthplace Shaped by Early Jupiter
bennu_samples_2026.summary: Analysis of half‑gram Bennu material shows it formed near the water‑ice line from mixed inner and outer Solar System dust, with Jupiter’s gravity directing the process.
highlights: Isotopic fingerprints of iron, titanium and chromium link Bennu to Ryugu and rare CI meteorites
The samples, collected by OSIRIS‑REx and delivered in 2023, total about 120 grams with half a gram examined by ETH Zurich
Researchers propose Jupiter’s early growth acted as a barrier, allowing fine dust to mix at the water‑ice line
Bennu’s composition suggests it retains the original elemental mix from which terrestrial planets later formed

150_million_year_old_bird_with_dinosaur_.headline: Jurassic Flightless Bird Yuezhuornis Shows Early Avian Diversity
150_million_year_old_bird_with_dinosaur_.summary: A 150‑million‑year‑old fossil from China reveals Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, a ground‑dwelling bird with dinosaur teeth and claws, marking the earliest known loss of flight.
highlights: Yuezhuornis lived in the Late Jurassic (150‑148 Ma) and is placed crownward of Archaeopteryx within Avialae.
Its jaws bear closely spaced serrated teeth and a sickle‑shaped second‑toe claw typical of deinonychosaurs.
Limb proportions match modern ground‑dwelling birds, indicating it was likely flightless.
The Nature paper employed maximum parsimony and Bayesian tip‑dating to resolve its phylogenetic position.

solar_magnetic_web_2026.headline: Sunrise‑III Balloon Telescope Reveals Hidden Magnetic Web Above Quiet Sun
solar_magnetic_web_2026.summary: Using the balloon‑borne Sunrise‑III observatory, scientists mapped delicate thread‑like magnetic structures and spicule fields in the quiet Sun’s chromosphere, exposing a complex magnetic canopy.
highlights: Thread‑like magnetic features were detected weaving through the chromosphere of a quiet solar region
Computer simulations linked surface twisting motions to the formation of the observed magnetic threads
Magnetic fields inside spicules were measured, showing how they evolve with height
The 1‑meter telescope operated at ~35 km altitude, achieving unprecedented magnetic resolution

glioblastoma_microenvironment_breakthrou.headline: Viscous Fluid Triggers Aggressive Behavior in Glioblastoma Cells
glioblastoma_microenvironment_breakthrou.summary: Researchers found that prolonged exposure to thick tumor fluid makes glioblastoma cells smaller, more flexible, and persistently more invasive, revealing a mechanical memory.
highlights: Cells exposed to 7.1 cP fluid became smaller and more deformable, enabling faster migration through narrow gaps
Adapted cells retained increased invasiveness even after returning to normal‑viscosity media
U‑251 cells activated mesenchymal genes CD44, FN1 and MMP9, while LN‑229 showed physical changes without major gene shifts
The open microfluidic chip allowed month‑long culture and direct observation of viscosity‑induced cellular memory

superconductor_flaw_2026.headline: Hidden Patchwork in Cuprate Superconductor Challenges Four Decades of Theory
superconductor_flaw_2026.summary: Advanced 3D X‑ray diffraction imaging reveals a complex patchwork of crystal domains and unusually wide boundaries that likely weaken superconductivity in a cuprate studied for 40 years.
highlights: Scanning 3D X‑ray diffraction at the upgraded European Synchrotron Radiation Facility mapped atomic structures inside the
The cuprate contains two slightly different atomic arrangements separated by transition zones hundreds of times wider than
These broad domain walls are predicted to impede electron flow, offering an explanation for performance variations among cuprate
Findings published in Physical Review Letters suggest existing bulk measurements may need reinterpretation and future theories

beijing_superpollutant_surging.headline: SF6 Emissions Surge in Beijing Amid AI‑Driven Chip Boom
beijing_superpollutant_surging.summary: A new study shows sulfur hexafluoride levels rising sharply in Beijing, driven by expanding power grids and fast‑growing semiconductor manufacturing despite overall air‑quality gains.
highlights: SF6 is 24,300 times more potent than CO₂ per kilogram
Electric power sector accounts for about 70 percent of Beijing’s SF6 emissions
Semiconductor manufacturing has become the region’s primary local SF6 source
State‑owned utilities recycle only ~30 percent of discarded SF6
The study analyzes atmospheric data from 1993‑2024

liver_disease_subtypes_2026.headline: MASLD May Consist of Five Distinct Subtypes With Varying Health Risks
liver_disease_subtypes_2026.summary: A Mayo Clinic analysis of 1,532 patients, validated in 3,070 others, identifies five MASLD subtypes linked to different long‑term disease outcomes.
highlights: Five MASLD subtypes (C1‑C5) show distinct profiles for liver cancer, transplant risk, and cardiovascular complications
Subtype C1 comprises about 30 percent of patients, older and non‑obese, with higher liver cancer rates
Subtype C5, representing roughly 9 percent, is driven largely by genetic factors
Patients were tracked for up to 10 years, revealing subtype‑specific risks for heart disease and liver failure

neocoast_2_ctdna_clearance_study.headline: Dato-DXd combo boosts ctDNA clearance and survival in resectable NSCLC
neocoast_2_ctdna_clearance_study.summary: In the phase‑2 NeoCOAST-2 trial, adding datopotamab deruxtecan to durvalumab and chemotherapy achieved the highest pathological complete response and ctDNA clearance, translating into superior 24‑month event‑free survival.
highlights: Arm 4 (Dato-DXd + durvalumab + chemo) reached 35.2% pathological complete response, the highest among arms.
ctDNA clearance at Cycle 3 Day 1 was 72.5% in Arm 4 versus 50.9% and 54.5% in Arms 1 and 2.
24‑month event‑free survival was 77.9% for Arm 4, compared with 70.5% and 75.7% in the other arms.
Combined ctDNA clearance and pCR predicted a ten‑fold reduction in risk of recurrence (HR 0.10).

laboratory_simulation_of_solar_explosion.headline: Lab‑Created Plasma Shows Magnetic Reconnection May Heat Solar Corona
laboratory_simulation_of_solar_explosion.summary: Chinese researchers reproduced magnetic reconnection in laser‑produced plasma, achieving electron temperatures near 820,000 °C, offering clues to the Sun’s coronal heating mystery.
highlights: Four overlapping laser beams struck a rippled plastic target at the Shenguang‑II laser facility, generating finger‑like plasma
Oppositely directed magnetic fields formed around the plasma fingers and reconnection doubled the peak electron temperature.
Comparative runs with a flat target produced only half the electron temperature, confirming the role of magnetic reconnection.
The experiment, published in Physical Review Letters, models conditions akin to solar nanoflares and coronal‑rain instabilities.

rare_lunar_meteorites_study.headline: Rare Lunar Meteorites Offer Broader Glimpse into Moon’s Evolution
rare_lunar_meteorites_study.summary: Lunar meteorites, representing only 0.7% of fallen meteorites, provide random sampling of the Moon’s surface, filling gaps left by Apollo and Chang’e missions.
highlights: Only 835 lunar meteorites have been verified, a tiny fraction of Earth‑falling rocks.
They originate from across the Moon, including the far side, unlike the geographically limited Apollo and Chang’e samples.
Researchers estimate tens to hundreds of kilograms of lunar material strike Earth each year, yet most remain undiscovered.
The rocks can test the lunar magma ocean hypothesis and probe the Moon’s highland crust formation.

sn_ares_a_strongly_lensed_type_iib_super.headline: SN Ares: First Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at z = 1.276 Shows 70‑Year Time Delay
sn_ares_a_strongly_lensed_type_iib_super.summary: Astronomers identified SN Ares, a Type IIb supernova at redshift 1.276, whose lensing by MACS J0308.9+2645 predicts a 70‑year repeat appearance for future observations.
highlights: JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy detected helium lines at 5876 Å, 7065 Å, and 10830 Å.
The supernova is classified as Type IIb, the highest‑redshift spectroscopic example of this class.
Lens modeling shows magnifications of ~5× for the first image and ~1.5× for the later images.
Predicted re‑appearance of SN Ares in ≥70 years will enable direct measurement of cosmological time delays.

gaia_dr3_compact_binary_candidates_const.headline: Torsional Alfvén Waves Transform into Magnetic Switchbacks in Simulated Coronal Hole
gaia_dr3_compact_binary_candidates_const.summary: A new arXiv simulation shows that surface‑driven torsional Alfvén waves steepen and generate cylindrical plasma jets, producing switchbacks in a ring configuration.
highlights: Simulations launch torsional Alfvén waves via surface rotation into a super‑radially expanding coronal‑hole field
Wave steepening and a parallel plasma jet combine to create magnetic switchbacks with characteristic ring geometry
Derived scaling laws predict peak deflection angles and length scales of the switchbacks
Results align with recent Parker Solar Probe observations of Alfvénic field reversals

finest_eos_supernovae.headline: Non‑monotonic Nucleon Effective Mass Drives Supernova Explosion Outcomes
finest_eos_supernovae.summary: New FINEST EOS tables, built from ab‑initio calculations and neutron‑star data, show that the density‑dependent nucleon effective mass strongly reshapes core‑collapse supernova dynamics.
highlights: FINEST EOS incorporates ab‑initio nuclear matter constraints and recent neutron‑star observations
Effective‑mass non‑monotonicity beyond saturation density alters proto‑neutron star contraction
Variations in incompressibility, symmetry energy, and high‑density pressure produce only modest early post‑bounce effects
High progenitor compactness amplifies the impact of effective‑mass behavior on explosion outcome

contributions_of_massive_stars_and_class.headline: Classical Novae May Dominate Galactic 26Al Production, Cutting Star‑Formation Rate Estimates
contributions_of_massive_stars_and_class.summary: Analysis of 20 years of INTEGRAL/SPI data suggests novae contribute 77‑84% of Galactic 26Al, reducing the inferred star‑formation rate to 1‑2 Msun yr⁻¹.
highlights: Novae account for up to 84% of the 1.8 MeV γ‑ray signal from 26Al
The revised 26Al contribution lowers the Galactic star‑formation rate to 1‑2 Msun yr⁻¹
Model fits reconcile the previously over‑predicted 60Fe/26Al ratio
Future MeV telescopes could resolve individual massive stars such as Gamma‑2‑Velorum

multiphase_gas_structure_in_jwst_little_.headline: JWST Reveals Multiphase Gas in Distant Little Red Dots
multiphase_gas_structure_in_jwst_little_.summary: JWST spectroscopy of eleven high‑redshift little red dots shows that dense clumps within hot ionized gas explain anomalous Hβ absorption.
highlights: Hβ absorption deeper than Hα cannot arise in a homogeneous medium
Radiative‑transfer modeling of 11 LRDs requires a multiphase structure
N_{HI,n=2} from Hα falls two orders of magnitude below Balmer‑break limits
Dense clumps embedded in diffuse hot ionized gas reconcile line and continuum data

saturn_co2_formation.headline: Saturn Likely Formed Near Carbon Dioxide Iceline, Study Finds
saturn_co2_formation.summary: A new one‑dimensional viscous α‑disk model shows Saturn’s heavy‑element makeup matches material accreted at the CO₂ iceline within the first 0.3 Myr.
highlights: Supersolar metallicities comparable to Saturn’s envelope appear only for disk turbulence α ≤ 10⁻³ at the CO₂ iceline
Carbon and phosphorus enrichments peak at ~0.2–0.3 Myr, matching Saturn’s atmospheric values
Noble‑gas abundances remain near protosolar because of long diffusion times

the_fate_of_ice_sheets_on_near_synchrono.headline: Near‑Synchronous Rotation Limits Ice Traps on M‑Dwarf Land Worlds
the_fate_of_ice_sheets_on_near_synchrono.summary: Using a 3D global climate model, researchers show that near‑synchronous spin reduces permanent nightside ice buildup on rocky exoplanets like TRAPPIST‑1e.
highlights: Permanent polar ice persists while lower‑latitude nightside ice grows with longer synodic days
An ice‑free dayside region can sustain liquid water in steady‑state simulations
Accounting for atmospheric lapse rate and isostatic adjustment cuts predicted ice accumulation by about a factor of 3

observational_evidence_of_the_gaia_encel.headline: Gaia‑Enceladus‑Sausage Merger Leaves Symmetric Imprint Across Galactic Center
observational_evidence_of_the_gaia_encel.summary: Analysis of 14,056 red giants shows the Gaia‑Enceladus‑Sausage’s metal‑rich component and high anisotropy also dominate the far side of the inner halo.
highlights: The far‑side halo hosts a metal‑rich peak at [Fe/H] ≈ –1.4, matching the near‑side signature.
Velocity anisotropy on the far side reaches β ≈ 0.8–0.9, characteristic of the GES “sausage” pattern.
Action‑space analysis attributes 10.86 % ± 0.23 % of far‑side stars to the GES merger, comparable to 11.56 % ± 0.16 % on the
Robust tests confirm the signal is not due to disk contamination or Sagittarius‑stream remnants.

dde_neutrino_correlations_desi.headline: DESI BAO Data Reveal Link Between Dynamical Dark Energy and Neutrino Masses
dde_neutrino_correlations_desi.summary: Joint analysis of DESI BAO, Planck CMB, and Pantheon+ supernovae shows a strong degeneracy between dark energy equation of state and relic neutrino mass.
highlights: DESI BAO measurements favor dynamical dark energy over the standard ΛCDM model
Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis of Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and Pantheon+ data finds a robust parameter degeneracy
The tight constraint on the CMB acoustic scale drives the correlation between dark energy and neutrino parameters
The study highlights the necessity of jointly constraining the neutrino sector and dark sector in next‑generation cosmological

jwst_lava_planet_toi561b.headline: JWST Finds Lava Planet TOI-561b Cloaked in Reflective Cloud Sunscreen
jwst_lava_planet_toi561b.summary: A scorching exoplanet 280 light‑years away reflects ~75% of starlight thanks to mineral clouds, suggesting a thick atmosphere sustained by a global lava ocean.
highlights: TOI-561b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, comparable to Venus
Mineral clouds of silicon dioxide and magnesium silicate likely act as a planetary sunscreen
Observations covered four full orbits using JWST/NIRSpec phase‑curve measurements
Atmosphere may be continuously replenished by gases from a global molten‑rock ocean

debris_disc_dead_star_double_disc.headline: Double Debris Disc Around White Dwarf Offers Glimpse of Solar System’s Future
debris_disc_dead_star_double_disc.summary: Astronomers using ESO’s VLT discovered a rare double-ring debris disc around white dwarf J1328‑1450, shaped by two surviving planetesimals, hinting at our Sun’s fate.
highlights: The disc consists of two concentric rings separated by a clear gap, unlike previously known single-ring white‑dwarf discs.
Spectroscopy with X‑Shooter reveals calcium, oxygen, magnesium and iron, with the inner ring enriched in magnesium gas.
The inner planetesimal is asteroid‑sized, while the outer body may be as large as Pluto or the Moon.
Study published in Nature Astronomy (doi:10.1038/s41550‑026‑03004‑3) provides the first evidence of complex debris structures

native_hawaiian_origin_genetics.headline: Genetic Study Traces Native Hawaiians to Rapa Nui, Reveals Founder Effects
native_hawaiian_origin_genetics.summary: Analysis of 1,050 Polynesian genomes shows Native Hawaiians share closest ancestry with Rapa Nui, highlighting severe founder‑effect bottlenecks and rare disease mutations.
highlights: Whole‑genome data from 1,050 individuals across French Polynesia, plus 12 Rapa Nui and NIH All of Us samples, were analyzed with
The closest genetic ties are between Native Hawaiians and Rapa Nui, despite 7,000 km separating the islands.
Founder‑effect bottlenecks reduced variation, concentrating rare recessive mutations in ADAMTSL4, PDE6B, and FAN1 among Native

bound_states_continuum.headline: Electronic Bound States in the Continuum Observed in Novel Metal
bound_states_continuum.summary: For the first time, researchers have directly observed electronic bound states in the continuum within the 2D metal Pd5AlI2 using scanning tunnelling microscopy.
highlights: Electronic BICs were identified at palladium vacancies in the tetragonal checkerboard lattice of Pd5AlI2.
Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy revealed the states are isolated from the metallic continuum despite the absence of a band gap.
When two defect sites are close, hybridization occurs, hinting at many‑body phenomena such as superconductivity.
The team plans to engineer BICs at predetermined locations, opening routes for quantum device design and catalysis.

electron_spin_macroscopic_motion.headline: Electron Spin Force Moves Centimeter‑Scale Diamond Sample
electron_spin_macroscopic_motion.summary: Physicists at Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology used polarized nitrogen‑vacancy spins to lift a 128‑milligram diamond by up to 1.5 µm in vacuum.
highlights: Spin polarization generated by green‑laser illumination produced a measurable upward force on the diamond.
The levitated graphite plate and interferometer tracked displacements of ~100 nm in air and ~1.5 µm in vacuum.
The experiment demonstrates that quantum spin forces can produce macroscopic motion, a step toward spatial Schrödinger‑cat states.

jak_inhibitors_viral_spread.headline: Common Anti‑Inflammatory JAK Inhibitors May Aid Virus Spread in Body
jak_inhibitors_viral_spread.summary: Researchers at NTNU found that widely used JAK inhibitor drugs suppress antiviral genes, allowing influenza, SARS‑CoV‑2 and other viruses to spread more easily.
highlights: JAK inhibitors such as baricitinib reduce activity of innate immune genes across lung, eye and brain organoids.
The effect was demonstrated for Rift Valley fever virus, influenza A, adenovirus and SARS‑CoV‑2.
Study published in NAR Molecular Medicine (peer‑reviewed 2025) and funded by Norwegian and Swedish research councils.
Authors advise caution prescribing JAK inhibitors during viral outbreaks.

2610_36486v1.headline: Three‑Flavor Neutrino Transport Reveals New Flavor Instabilities in Neutron‑Star Merger Remnants
2610_36486v1.summary: Axisymmetric general‑relativistic three‑flavor Boltzmann simulations show widespread collisional and fast flavor instabilities, reshaping neutrino emission in long‑lived merger remnants.
highlights: Linear stability analysis finds strong CFI across all three flavor sectors, including narrow resonance‑like structures.
Muonic interactions shift the $e\tau$ fast flavor instability toward denser disk regions compared with two‑flavor models.
Disk demuonization creates a $\nu_\mu$ excess and asymmetric lepton‑number angular distributions that suppress FFI in $e\mu$ and
Three‑flavor quantum kinetic equation calculations reveal nonlinear coupling that excites coherence even in initially stable

2610_37383v1.headline: ACT and SPT data tighten limits on single-field inflation models
2610_37383v1.summary: New analysis shows that only specific single-field inflation potentials can boost sub‑Mpc perturbations while staying within the ACT/SPT scalar spectral index constraints.
highlights: Bump/dip‑modified, step‑like, and double‑inflection‑point potentials each fit within the 2σ range of the measured scalar
Models can simultaneously satisfy ACT/SPT CMB data and recent pulsar‑timing array (PTA) observations
Achieving the required small‑scale enhancement remains difficult when primordial black‑hole (PBH) abundance limits are imposed

2610_36446v1.headline: Giant Impacts May Help Rocky Worlds Keep Their Primordial Atmospheres
2610_36446v1.summary: New modeling shows that post‑disk giant collisions increase gravitational binding more than mantle heating, favoring retention of hydrogen‑rich envelopes on Earth‑sized planets.
highlights: Impacts add the entire accreted mass to a planet’s gravitational binding energy.
Only a fraction of impact energy heats the mantle; latent heat of melting absorbs much of it.
Larger, atmosphere‑bearing planets are more likely to survive giant impacts than smaller, atmosphere‑less ones.
Population models predict sub‑Neptunes possess more massive rocky interiors than super‑Earths.

pah_jwst_ngc4151.headline: JWST Detects Resilient PAH Emission Near Seyfert Nucleus of NGC 4151
pah_jwst_ngc4151.summary: JWST NIRSpec/IFU spectroscopy reveals 3.3 µm PAH emission within 200 pc of NGC 4151, persisting down to 50 pc despite AGN radiation in the galaxy.
highlights: PAH 3.3 µm line detected as close as ~50 pc from the active nucleus.
Surface brightness of PAH emission rises toward the nucleus, implying AGN‑driven UV excitation.
No PAH signal found within the narrow line region, suggesting destruction by ionized outflows.
Findings challenge prior models that small PAH grains cannot survive near luminous AGN.

evidence_for_a_nova_super_remnant_surrou.headline: eROSITA Detects Nova Super-Remnant Around Recurrent Nova V745 Scorpii
evidence_for_a_nova_super_remnant_surrou.summary: Using eROSITA data, astronomers identified an X‑ray shell matching a nova super‑remnant surrounding the Galactic recurrent nova V745 Scorpii.
highlights: The X‑ray shell aligns with the position of V745 Scorpii and spans a size comparable to known NSRs.
Infrared observations reveal a cavity coincident with the X‑ray structure, supporting a remnant origin.
Radial emission profiles closely resemble those of the confirmed NSR around M31N 2008‑12a.
Simulations predict such shells should accompany all recurrent novae, making this the first NSR detected via X‑rays.

smbhb_2to1_harmonics.institution: University of Michigan / Owens Valley Radio Observatory
smbhb_2to1_harmonics.headline: 2:1 Harmonics Detected in Radio Light Curves of SMBH Binary Candidates
smbhb_2to1_harmonics.summary: Researchers report 2:1 periodic harmonics in the radio monitoring data of two supermassive black‑hole binary candidates, strengthening evidence for coherent blazar variability.
highlights: PKS J0805-0111 and PKS 2131-021 show matching 2:1 harmonic periods in OVRO and UMRAO data
A similar 2:1 harmonic was previously found in candidate J1309+1154
Four theoretical models are proposed to explain the commensurable periodicities
The observed periods exceed two years and can vanish over long monitoring spans

earths_ice_ages_hidden_ocean_chain_react.headline: Northern Ice Sheets May Have Triggered Antarctic Carbon Sink, New Study Finds
earths_ice_ages_hidden_ocean_chain_react.summary: Computer simulations show that cooling from expanding northern ice sheets can drive Southern Ocean changes that draw down atmospheric CO2, potentially amplifying past ice ages.
highlights: Isolated Northern Hemisphere cooling produced 74% of the CO2 drawdown achieved by global cooling in the model.
The mechanism links North Atlantic cooling to altered circulation around Antarctica, enhancing ocean carbon storage.
Study published in the peer‑reviewed Journal of Climate using an idealized ocean model.
Lead author Dr. Madison Shankle and colleagues at University of St Andrews propose this hidden chain reaction explains ice‑age

uranus_neptune_origin_study.headline: Uranus Formed In‑Place While Neptune’s Building Blocks Migrated Outward
uranus_neptune_origin_study.summary: A peer‑reviewed study shows that Uranus formed where it is today, whereas Neptune’s material originated much closer to the Sun before moving outward.
highlights: Uranus formed locally, but Neptune’s building blocks condensed near the Sun
ALMA measurements revealed a higher oxygen abundance in Neptune’s atmosphere
Models of the protoplanetary disk indicate distinct chemical reservoirs for the two planets
The findings rely on carbon monoxide tracers and were published in Astronomy & Astrophysics

hidden_volcanic_system_iran.headline: Hidden 100‑Million‑Year‑Old Volcanic Arc Uncovered in Northwestern Iran
hidden_volcanic_system_iran.summary: An international team led by Istanbul Technical University identified a Late Cretaceous continental magmatic arc in northwestern Iran, revealing a missing piece of Neo‑Tethys history.
highlights: Zircon U‑Pb dating shows the arc formed 101–97 Ma during Neo‑Tethys reorganization.
Hf isotope and whole‑rock geochemistry confirm continental arc magmatism.
The Siah Cheshmeh‑Khoy‑Misho‑Tabriz Fault likely marks the tectonic boundary of the arc.
Discovery adds a third magmatic arc to Iran’s Late Cretaceous record alongside Sananda‑Sirjan and Urumieh‑Dokhtar arcs.

how_spiders_spin_silk_dope_into_nature_s.headline: Scientists Reveal Condensate Phase Driving Spider Silk’s Super‑Strength
how_spiders_spin_silk_dope_into_nature_s.summary: Researchers mapped how phosphate‑triggered condensates reorganize spidroin proteins into beta‑sheet fibers, explaining spider silk’s exceptional strength and guiding biomimetic material design.
