highlights: The 10‑meter South Pole Telescope exploits a radio‑quiet atmospheric window to map gravitational‑lensing B‑modes.
BICEP Array, now in its fifth generation, targets the ultra‑weak B‑mode signal from quantum‑origin gravitational waves.
Collaboration between SPT and BICEP combines large‑scale sensitivity with precise lensing maps, reducing systematic contamination.
Previous BICEP2 claims of inflationary B‑modes were later attributed to Milky Way dust, underscoring the need for

velocity_reconstruction_from_ksz_with_sp.headline: South Pole Telescope Achieves First Velocity Reconstruction via kSZ with DESI Data
velocity_reconstruction_from_ksz_with_sp.summary: Using SPT-3G maps and DESI Legacy Imaging Survey galaxies, researchers detect galaxy‑velocity correlations and velocity power spectrum, constraining primordial non‑Gaussianity.
highlights: Galaxy‑velocity correlation detected with signal‑to‑noise ratio 11.2 across 95‑220 GHz bands
Velocity power spectrum measured with signal‑to‑noise ratio 8.1, including first detection at 220 GHz
Reconstructed velocities provide new constraints on local‑type primordial non‑Gaussianity, yielding fₙₗ=‑38⁺⁶¹_‑61
Foreground modeling separates thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich effect and cosmic infrared background contributions

2611_22417v1.headline: Relativistic Tidal Excitation of g‑ and i‑Modes Could Reveal Neutron Star Interiors
2611_22417v1.summary: A fully relativistic scattering study shows that crust‑core interface i‑modes may produce detectable gravitational‑wave phase shifts, while g‑modes remain elusive.
highlights: Crust‑core i‑modes with high shear speeds generate the largest predicted phase shifts
Direct g‑mode excitation stays below detection thresholds even for strong stratification
Hadron‑quark interface i‑modes are unlikely to be observed with next‑generation detectors

gw_calibration_o4.headline: Global Photon Calibrator Standards Sharpened for O4 Gravitational‑Wave Run
gw_calibration_o4.summary: During the O4 observing run, improved photon‑calibrator reference standards from NIST and PTB boosted calibration accuracy across the worldwide gravitational‑wave detector network.
highlights: A three‑year NIST‑PTB bilateral comparison established tighter laser power standards for photon calibrators.
Transfer standards calibrated at NIST and PTB were propagated to reference power sensors at each observatory.
Calibration uncertainties were reduced, enhancing the precision of high‑signal‑to‑noise gravitational‑wave detections.

2611_22387v1.headline: Velocity‑Dependent Dark Matter Annihilation Leaves Distinct Imprints on Cosmic Gamma‑Ray Maps
2611_22387v1.summary: A new halo‑model analysis shows that velocity‑dependent WIMP annihilation produces unique signatures in the unresolved gamma‑ray background when cross‑correlated with large‑scale structure.
highlights: Researchers model annihilation cross section as σv∝vⁿ for n = –1, 0, 2, 4.
Velocity dependence shifts the dominant halo mass range and alters effective bias and redshift distribution.
Forecasts using Fermi‑LAT UGRB and 2MRS galaxies predict detectable differences between s‑wave and Sommerfeld‑like scenarios.
Cross‑correlation method complements traditional gamma‑ray intensity searches, tightening constraints on dark‑matter particle

14.headline: Supernova 1987A Sets New Tight Limit on Neutrino Magnetic Dipole Moment
14.summary: A reanalysis of SN 1987A data using modern supernova simulations and Galactic magnetic field models limits Dirac electron neutrino dipole moments to ≤ 4.8 × 10⁻¹³ μ_B.
highlights: Production of sterile neutrinos in supernova cores via electromagnetic plasma fluctuations.
Updated calculations include scattering on both protons and electrons.
Incorporates latest SN simulation data and detailed Milky Way magnetic‑field modeling.
Sets bound μ_{ν_e} ≲ 4.8 × 10⁻¹³ μ_B, surpassing previous terrestrial and astrophysical limits.

juno_cpc_structure.headline: Juno Microwave Radiometer Maps 3‑D Structure of Jupiter’s Polar Cyclones
juno_cpc_structure.summary: Juno’s microwave data from 2023‑2024 reveal that northern cyclones have modest ammonia depletion near 5 bar and warm‑core signatures, unlike the central cyclone.
highlights: Eight northern cyclones show enhanced microwave brightness and ~5 bar ammonia depletion.
Five cyclones exhibit twice the ammonia loss and deeper localized heating than the other three.
The central polar cyclone displays little microwave contrast despite its cloudy appearance in visible and infrared images.
Findings suggest CPCs and the central cyclone arise from distinct dynamical regimes, challenging prior models.

new_discovery_reveals_what_may_be_holdin.headline: Room‑Temperature Pairing Found, Phase Coherence Remains Key Barrier
new_discovery_reveals_what_may_be_holdin.summary: Scientists at Utrecht, Leiden and Munich showed electron pairs can survive at room temperature, revealing phase coherence as the remaining obstacle to superconductivity.
highlights: Electron pairs persist at everyday temperatures in a cuprate material
The pairing energy matches the pseudogap, confirming a long‑sought equivalence
Phase coherence, not pairing, is identified as the bottleneck for superconductivity

fermi_mev_gap_catalog.headline: Fermi LAT’s 14‑Year Survey Reveals 450 Sources Closing the MeV Gap
fermi_mev_gap_catalog.summary: An analysis of 14 years of Fermi LAT data identified 450 gamma‑ray sources between 20 and 200 MeV, delivering the clearest low‑energy view yet.
highlights: The Second Catalog of Low‑Energy Fermi‑LAT Sources (2FLE) lists 450 distinct objects in the 20‑200 MeV band.
Flat‑spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) dominate, accounting for nearly half of the extragalactic detections.
52 Galactic sources are found, mostly pulsars, with a possible first gamma‑ray detection from the globular cluster M2.
73 sources lack counterparts, including 60 entirely new gamma‑ray emitters, hinting at unknown cosmic accelerators.

space_dust_heavy_water.headline: Kuiper Belt Dust Confirms Hidden Reservoir of Heavy Water Beyond Neptune
space_dust_heavy_water.summary: Analysis of twelve interplanetary dust grains collected by NASA’s Cosmic Dust program shows the outer solar system harbored water enriched in oxygen‑17 and oxygen‑18.
highlights: Twelve dust grains displayed radiation tracks indicating Kuiper Belt origins.
Clay minerals in the grains reveal liquid water activity on their parent bodies.
Oxygen isotope ratios confirm extreme enrichment of ^17O and ^18O compared to inner‑solar system material.
Saturn’s early‑disk pressure ridge likely prevented heavy water from migrating inward.

homo_erectus_denisovan_coexistence_china.institution: Chinese research teams (e.g., Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology)
homo_erectus_denisovan_coexistence_china.headline: Late Homo erectus survived in southern China alongside Denisovans, study shows
homo_erectus_denisovan_coexistence_china.summary: Nine fossil teeth from Guangxi caves reveal Homo erectus lived in rainforest China until about 184,000 years ago, possibly overlapping with Denisovan populations.
highlights: Radiometric dating places the teeth between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago.
Proteomic analysis confirmed four teeth as Homo erectus and identified a mysterious ninth tooth likely Denisovan.
Isotopic data show the Homo erectus group exploited tropical plants and animals in rainforest habitats.
Strontium signatures link the individuals to karst landscapes spanning southern China and northern Vietnam.

mit_discovers_that_aging_weakens_the_bra.headline: Aging Weakens Brain’s Nighttime Cleaning Waves, Study Finds
mit_discovers_that_aging_weakens_the_bra.summary: MIT researchers found that older adults show significantly weaker cerebrospinal fluid waves during deep sleep, linked to reduced brain blood flow and slower electrical activity.
highlights: Older participants (60‑84) exhibited markedly smaller CSF flow waves than younger adults (18‑39) during non‑REM sleep
Weaker CSF waves correlated with diminished neurovascular coupling and blunted cerebral blood‑flow responses
Some older adults retained youthful CSF wave amplitudes, suggesting protective factors
Findings published in Nature Aging and may inform early detection of dementia risk

andromeda_stellar_merger.headline: Andromeda Giant Star Merger Caught in Real Time
andromeda_stellar_merger.summary: A giant star in the Andromeda galaxy brightened for years before a dramatic eruption in October 2025 revealed a merger of two stars, reported in Nature.
highlights: The brightening began in 2018 and continued for seven years, reaching twice the star’s original size.
Researchers identified the binary as Little Bao orbiting inside Big Bao, a classic common‑envelope evolution scenario.
Only about ten percent of the giant’s outer gas escaped during the October 2025 eruption, indicating a full merger.
The study used nearly 30 years of telescope data and was led by Viraj Karambelkar at Columbia University.

cee_observation_2025abao.headline: First Direct Observation of Common‑Envelope Inspiral in Andromeda Galaxy
cee_observation_2025abao.summary: Astronomers observed AT 2025abao in the Andromeda Galaxy, capturing a ~0.7 M⊙ companion spiralling inside a ~7 M⊙ AGB star’s envelope over seven years.
highlights: Pre‑ and post‑eruption spectra show a ~0.7 M⊙ companion inspiralling within a ~7 M⊙ AGB envelope.
Brightening lasted ~seven years, matching predicted frictional drag energy dissipation.
Merger ejected ~10% of the envelope at speeds ~10 × the primary’s escape velocity.
The efficiency of orbital energy conversion to envelope ejection is constrained to 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4.

dual_quasar_tsz_2026.headline: Dual Quasar at z 2.37 Powers Massive Hot Gas Bubble
dual_quasar_tsz_2026.summary: Astronomers detect a 6 σ thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich signal around a dual quasar at z = 2.37, revealing a hot gas bubble with ≈ 9.7×10⁶⁰ erg of thermal energy.
highlights: Thermal Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich (tSZ) decrement detected at 6 σ in millimeter wavelengths
Hot gas thermal energy estimated at 9.7×10⁶⁰ erg, exceeding expectations for a 10¹³ M⊙ halo by 3.6‑fold
Bubble size spans 100‑600 kpc, implying quasar‑driven outflows on intergalactic scales

massive_outer_companion_toi_178.headline: Massive Brown Dwarf Companion Discovered Orbiting Resonant Chain Star TOI-178
massive_outer_companion_toi_178.summary: A massive outer companion, likely a brown dwarf of ~21 Jupiter masses, has been detected around TOI-178, which hosts a six‑planet resonant chain.
highlights: Gaia DR2/DR3‑Hipparcos astrometry combined with radial velocities reveals the outer object
Posterior orbital fit gives semi‑major axis ~6.9 AU and eccentricity ~0.76
High‑contrast imaging limits rule out stellar companions, supporting a brown‑dwarf classification
N‑body simulations show the inner resonant chain remains stable despite the perturbation

arxiv_2611_24509v1.headline: Analytical Equation Maps Ultralight Dark Matter Halo Formation
arxiv_2611_24509v1.summary: Researchers derive a fully analytical equation describing how ultralight boson dark matter halos evolve, tracking size and density through cosmic expansion and quantum pressure effects.
highlights: First fully analytical time‑evolution equation for perturbations into isolated halos
Applies time‑dependent variational analysis to simplify halo formation dynamics
Identifies background density, Universe expansion, and quantum pressure as key regulators of halo size and density

spherical_nn_primordial_gw.headline: Spherical Neural Network Sharpens Primordial Gravitational Wave Search in CMB Maps
spherical_nn_primordial_gw.summary: A spherical graph convolutional network directly infers the tensor-to-scalar ratio r from multifrequency CMB B‑mode maps, outperforming traditional likelihood methods.
highlights: The network reduces rms error on r by a factor of 1.3 compared with a multifrequency bandpower likelihood.
It yields 68% confidence intervals 1.2 times narrower using the same prior.
Training used 20,000 simulated sky realizations including lensed CMB, dust and synchrotron foregrounds.
Saliency maps reveal the model automatically favors the deepest, cleanest sky regions and frequency channels.

very_massive_stars_metal_poor_galaxies.headline: Search Finds No Very Massive Stars in Ultra‑Metal‑Poor Galaxies
very_massive_stars_metal_poor_galaxies.summary: Analysis of optical and new UV spectra from nearby galaxies with Z ≲ 0.1 Z⊙ reveals no evidence of candidate Very Massive Stars.
highlights: Selected galaxies show nebular He II λ4686 emission but lack Wolf‑Rayet bumps, making them prime VMS candidates.
Stellar wind features appear in only half the sample, and age estimates exceed the VMS lifetime.
Photoionization models using pySTARBURST99 and GALAXEV cannot reproduce observed line ratios without extreme parameters.
The study suggests multiple ionizing sources, not VMS, dominate the nebular emission.

low_cost_glass_scintillator.headline: Low‑Cost Gadolinium Oxyfluoride Glass Scintillator Shows Multimodal Radiation Detection Promise
low_cost_glass_scintillator.summary: A cerium‑doped gadolinium oxyfluoride glass developed by researchers at Wuhan University of Technology delivers high light yield across X‑rays, gamma rays, neutrons, muons and pions.
highlights: Achieves 85.5% energy transfer efficiency from gadolinium ions to cerium dopants.
Produces strong light signals suitable for hadronic calorimeters in high‑energy physics.
Reaches 29.8 lp/mm spatial resolution for X‑ray imaging, near the best reported for glass scintillators.
Uses a borosilicate scaffold with GdF3 to increase density while maintaining scintillation performance.

arctic_waters_reshape_life.headline: Arctic Sea Ice Loss Triggers Acidification and Food‑Web Shifts Across Pacific
arctic_waters_reshape_life.summary: Long‑term DBO data reveal that reduced sea ice increases CO₂ uptake, acidifies waters and alters benthic and whale food sources, threatening Indigenous harvests.
highlights: Sea ice decline extends ocean‑atmosphere exposure, boosting CO₂ absorption and lowering pH
Winter sampling by the Distributed Biological Observatory captured late‑season CO₂ spikes missed by summer cruises
Benthic surveys show shrinking clam and amphipod sizes, forcing gray whales to relocate feeding grounds
Indigenous communities report reduced availability of culturally important species such as walrus and bowhead whales

plant_based_mycotoxins_study.headline: All 212 UK Plant‑Based Foods Tested Contain Mycotoxins, Study Finds
plant_based_mycotoxins_study.summary: Researchers from University of Parma and Cranfield University detected at least one mycotoxin in every of 212 UK vegan and vegetarian products, though levels remained below EU limits.
highlights: Every one of the 212 surveyed plant‑based meat alternatives and beverages contained at least one of 19 mycotoxins.
All detected concentrations were under the European Union safety thresholds for mycotoxins.
The study was published in Food Control and funded by the Horizon Europe FunShield4Med project.
Authors plan further risk assessments linking dietary patterns to cumulative mycotoxin exposure.

deep_sea_pig_bacterium.headline: Tiny Bacterium Dominates Body Wall of Deep‑Sea Sea Pigs
deep_sea_pig_bacterium.summary: Researchers at University of Tokyo identified Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola, a genome‑tiny bacterium occupying over 70% of sea pig body‑wall microbes.
highlights: Genome size only 649,000 bases, about one‑seventh of Escherichia coli
27.6% of its DNA encodes giant surface proteins exceeding 5,000 amino acids
Fluorescence imaging located the bacterium within the body‑wall tissues of eight sea pigs
The bacterium lacks key energy‑generation genes, suggesting heavy reliance on its host
